name: icon
description: One glyph from the registry, at a size and a tone the system names. Every icon on every surface is this — the geometry lives once in `icons.avenceo.json` and a view supplies only a name, because the engine's tag allowlist admits no SVG and loosening it would let a view emit script. What this unit adds is the part the registry deliberately does not hold: how big, and in what colour, since geometry has no opinion about either.

base.$description: Sized in `em`, so an icon inside a control scales with that control rather than being pinned to a pixel value that is right in one place and wrong in the next. The DEFAULT is `lg` at 2rem — the type scale here tops out at 38px and bottoms at 9px, so an icon matched to body text lands at 13px, which is smaller than any glyph with a duotone backing can carry. An icon set inline beside a sentence should ask for `sm`. `flex-shrink:0` because a glyph is never the thing that should give way in a tight row.

size.$description: A ladder in rem rather than in type steps, because an icon is a shape and the type scale is a reading ladder — matching them made every icon smaller than the thing it labelled.

tone.$description: An icon inherits `currentColor` by default, which is right almost everywhere — it is part of the sentence it sits in. These are for the cases where it is not: a status glyph that must carry its own meaning.

a11y.note: Decorative by default — `aria-hidden`, because an icon beside a label that already says the word makes a screen reader say it twice. Give it a `title` ONLY when the icon is the whole message, at which point it becomes `role=img` with a label. An icon-only button is the other case: the label belongs on the button, not on the glyph inside it. Colour is never the only signal: a red error glyph needs the word too.
